clue.text: Filled by gatherings of the absent-minded in the upper house ?

definitions.text: Filled by gatherings of the absent-minded in the upper house ?

parts.words: Filled by gatherings of the absent-minded in the upper house
parts.note: the Lord Chancellor's seat in the House of Lords is a cushion stuffed with fleece, and the absent-minded are said to be wool-gathering

explanation.surface: Dozing peers fill the benches of the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gatherings of the absent-minded' are wool-gatherings, i.e. wool, which stuffs the Speaker's seat of the House of Lords, Britain's upper house.
explanation.definitionFit: The cushion on which the Lord Chancellor sits in the Lords is stuffed with fleece, hence its name.

clue.text: Trebly sticky ?

parts.note: a cricket target has three stumps, and a difficult pitch is called sticky

explanation.surface: Something gluey three times over.
explanation.walkthrough: A sticky wicket is a hard situation; in cricket, a British bat-and-ball game, the wicket has three stumps, so it is sticky three times.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket target is made of three stumps, and a damp pitch hard to bat on is the proverbial sticky one.

clue.text: Or emptied some dull — to the drains" (Keats)

definitions.text: Or emptied some dull — to the drains" (Keats)

parts.words: Or emptied some dull — to the drains" (Keats)
parts.note: the gap in this line of Ode to a Nightingale is filled by a sleep-inducing drug

explanation.surface: A quotation from Keats with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is from Keats's Ode to a Nightingale: 'Or emptied some dull opiate to the drains'.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats speaks of draining a narcotic draught, a drug derived from the poppy.

clue.text: A toady, though shy, can't possibly be out of work

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A bootlicker, however bashful, cannot afford to be unemployed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges SHY and CANT with OP (work); 'be out of' says the answer is made from them.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatterer who fawns on the powerful is a toady.

clue.text: Dr. Jekyll's laboratory ?

parts.note: Stevenson's doctor drank his potion there and turned into Mr Hyde

explanation.surface: Where Stevenson's doctor worked.
explanation.walkthrough: Jekyll's laboratory is where he changed into Hyde; a sports pavilion's room for putting on kit has the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sports clubs have a room for swapping clothes, and Jekyll transformed himself into Hyde in his.

clue.text: Port control and crime detection experts are unruffled

parts.note: the PLA is the Port of London Authority, which controls the Thames port
the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Harbour authorities and police detectives stay calm under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm and unflustered, the way a still pond is unruffled.

clue.text: Takes precedence on the housetops

explanation.surface: Something comes first up on the rooftops.
explanation.walkthrough: Leads are sheets of lead metal covering a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: To go first is to head the field; roofs are covered with sheets of the grey metal called by the same name.

clue.text: Pluck is half the battle

parts.note: pluck means cull, and those four letters make up the first half of the name of a Scottish battle

explanation.surface: Courage wins half of every fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pluck' seems to mean courage, but it means CULL, the front half of CULLODEN, the 1746 battle that ended the Jacobite rising in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The battle on Drummossie Moor in 1746 defeated Bonnie Prince Charlie's army.

clue.text: Spread for Pluto by himself

parts.note: Dis is another name for Pluto, Roman god of the underworld
per se is Latin for by itself or by himself

explanation.surface: The underworld god spreads himself on his own.
explanation.definitionFit: To scatter something in every direction is to spread it.

clue.text: Little girl meets Tom in Paris for small talk

parts.note: a chit is a slip of a girl
a tomcat in French is chat

explanation.surface: A young girl chats with Tom on a trip to Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom is a tomcat, not a man; in French a cat is CHAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle gossip and light conversation are small talk.

clue.text: Furs to suit Hamlet

explanation.surface: Clothing chosen to fit the Prince of Denmark.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet says 'I'll have a suit of sables', so these furs suit him in both senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable pelts are prized furs; Hamlet asks for a suit of these dark skins in the play.

clue.text: Bolt of the runaway rider

parts.note: mounted archers of ancient Parthia loosed arrows backwards while fleeing

explanation.surface: A horseman's mount suddenly runs off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' looks like a horse bolting; it is an arrow fired by a retreating horseman, now any cutting remark made on leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Retreating Parthian cavalry fired back at pursuers, so a parting barb bears their name.

clue.text: Goes to pot in this bar

indicators.note: the run of letters sits inside this stretch of the clue, 'goes to pot', across its words

explanation.surface: A pub goes to rack and ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across gOES TO Pot. 'Bar' is the legal sense: an estoppel bars a party from denying something.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, to estop is to bar or preclude someone from making a claim.

clue.text: The premier bagman

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister is a travelling salesman.
explanation.walkthrough: W.E. Gladstone was Victoria's Prime Minister, and the leather travelling bag is named after him, making him the bag's man.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladstone served as British Prime Minister four times, and a hinged leather portmanteau bears his name.

clue.text: Troupers, or troopers, with a rustic objective ?

explanation.surface: Touring actors, or soldiers attacking a farm building.
explanation.walkthrough: Travelling players who performed in barns were barnstormers; read literally, they are troops storming a barn.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnstorming players toured country districts giving shows; soldiers assaulting a farm building would literally storm a barn.

clue.text: Car Eleven needs change of bearing

indicators.note: the words car and eleven need their letters changed round

explanation.surface: Racing car number eleven must alter its course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' is not a direction but 'bearing on', pertinence.
explanation.definitionFit: Pertinence to a matter, having a bearing on it.

clue.text: Fatal frame-up

parts.note: the condemned climb up a wooden framework to the gallows

explanation.surface: A deadly piece of fraud against an innocent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frame-up' suggests a false accusation; it is a frame one goes up to be executed.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised platform for executions is the deadly framework climbed by the condemned.

clue.text: Dreadnought ?

parts.note: split as dread nought, the battleship's name means dreading nothing

explanation.surface: A big-gunned battleship.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'dread nought', the battleship becomes a description of someone afraid of nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dreads nothing is bold and unafraid.

clue.text: Marmion's charger heads all horses racing in Derbyshire

indicators.note: one piece heads the other, so the charger's name comes in front

parts.note: in Scott's poem Marmion the dying hero cries 'Charge, Chester, charge!'
the field is all the runners in a race

explanation.surface: A war-horse from Scott's poem leads the runners in a race held in Derbyshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charger' looks like a horse, but it is whoever Marmion urged to charge. CHESTERFIELD is a town in Derbyshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Chesterfield is a market town in that Midlands county, known for its crooked spire.

clue.text: Worker from the Oriental Oil Co.?

indicators.note: the worker is formed from the letters of the words that follow, rearranged

parts.note: E for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: An employee of an Eastern oil company.
explanation.walkthrough: E (Oriental) with OIL and CO are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired unskilled labourer in Asia was called by this term, now considered offensive.

clue.text: At five a girl is got up by a slave

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five

indicators.note: in a down entry, getting up means the word girl's synonym reads upwards

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: At five o'clock a young woman rises, woken by a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is got up' turns LASS into SSAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal tenant bound to serve a lord is a servile underling.

clue.text: They were victimized if not passed over

definitions.text: They were victimized if not passed over

parts.words: They were victimized if not passed over
parts.note: in Exodus the angel of death killed the eldest son of each Egyptian household it did not pass over

explanation.surface: Those not overlooked for promotion paid for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passed over' suggests being overlooked; it is the Passover, when only marked houses were spared.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenth plague of Egypt struck down eldest children in every house the angel did not pass over.

clue.text: Piece of equipment one is supplied with on guard

annotationWithheld.why: Piece of equipment one is supplied with on guard: no parse found for THONG from 'one is supplied with on guard'; neither the scan nor a reading gives T, H, O, N, G from those words
annotationWithheld.clue: Piece of equipment one is supplied with on guard

clue.text: Musical flower like Patience on a monument

explanation.surface: A tuneful bloom sits as still as a statue of Patience.
explanation.walkthrough: In Twelfth Night Viola describes a lovelorn girl who 'sat like Patience on a monument'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a stringed instrument, a pansy-like bloom, and the Shakespeare heroine who speaks of Patience on a monument.

clue.text: The senior officer with the eastern bunch is a beast !

parts.note: OC is Officer Commanding, the senior officer of a unit
E is the abbreviation for eastern
a lot is a bunch or group

explanation.surface: A commanding officer with his oriental troop behaves like an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A spotted American wild cat is a beast of the jungle.

clue.text: Complaint of roof-workers and hairdressers

explanation.surface: A grievance shared by roofers and barbers.
explanation.walkthrough: Roofers lay wooden tiles called shingles, and a shingle was a short tapered haircut of the 1920s.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a painful viral rash, and also wooden roof tiles and short bobbed haircuts.

clue.text: Same again, wise guy — it's what the doctor ordered

parts.note: do is short for ditto, meaning the same again
a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: Ordering the same again, a smart alec says it is just what the doctor prescribed.
explanation.definitionFit: A prescribed amount of medicine is what the physician orders.

clue.text: Where the real appears a bit airy-fairy

indicators.note: the letters show up spelt out within the words 'where the real' across their joins

explanation.surface: Reality turns up somewhere rather fanciful.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is wherE THE REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicate, light and unworldly, as airy-fairy notions are.
